events.title: Indonesia Declares Independence
events.description: Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaimed Indonesian independence in Jakarta, just days after Japan's surrender in World War II, beginning a four-year struggle against Dutch efforts to reassert colonial control.
events.significance: Marked the birth of the Republic of Indonesia, now the world's fourth most populous nation, and became a landmark moment in the post-war wave of decolonization in Asia.

events.title: First Transatlantic Balloon Crossing
events.description: Ben Abruzzo, Maxie Anderson, and Larry Newman landed the helium balloon Double Eagle II in Miserey, France, after departing Presque Isle, Maine, on August 11, completing the first manned balloon flight across the Atlantic Ocean.
events.significance: Achieved a long-sought aviation milestone that had defeated many earlier attempts, demonstrating the possibilities of long-distance ballooning.

events.title: Gabon Gains Independence from France
events.description: Gabon became an independent republic on August 17, 1960, ending its status as a French colony in Equatorial Africa, with Léon M'ba serving as its first prime minister and later president.
events.significance: Part of the 1960 wave of African independence, often called the Year of Africa, when seventeen nations gained independence from colonial rule.

events.title: Clinton Admits Relationship with Monica Lewinsky
events.description: President Bill Clinton testified before a grand jury via video link and then addressed the nation, admitting that he had an inappropriate relationship with White House intern Monica Lewinsky.
events.significance: The admission intensified the scandal that led to Clinton's impeachment by the House of Representatives in December 1998 and his acquittal by the Senate in 1999.

events.title: Izmit Earthquake in Turkey
events.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck northwestern Turkey near Izmit in the early morning hours, devastating densely populated and industrial areas including towns near Istanbul.
events.significance: Killed more than 17,000 people and left hundreds of thousands homeless, prompting major reforms in Turkey's building codes and disaster preparedness, and fostering Greek-Turkish goodwill through aid exchanges.
